knownObservation.interpretation: Separate hops; not proof of provider-hop encryption.

explicitUserDecision.meaning: Accept provider-managed unverified upstream risk and capacity/timeout operational residual risk for C3B only; request design/approval proposal, not implementation or execution.
explicitUserDecision.proposalBooleans: approved=false and executionAuthorized=false are retained. They do not deny the recorded user decision and do not grant operation authority.

conditions: Actual client TLS proof required separately for each psql/pg_dump/pg_dumpall invocation.
TLS verify-full with hostname and trusted CA verification remains mandatory; no profile/host/port override.
Keep backend observation as true/false/unavailable without converting it into client TLS authority.
Preserve existing snapshot/restore validation, finite plans, atomic migration/ledger and no automatic retry.
Risk acceptance does not approve a migration, backup, capture retry, plan seal, deployment or future maintenance.

expiryEnforcementDesign.perInvocation: Future strict operator authorization binds risk ID/raw artifact hash, C3B release ID, stageActive=true, completionObserved=false and existing <=900-second window. No operator authorization generated now.
expiryEnforcementDesign.closedMarker: Fixed receiptRoot/R7D-C3B.release-completed.json, if present (including malformed/unsafe entries), denies subsequent operations; never automatically delete or overwrite.
expiryEnforcementDesign.operatorBoundary: The trusted release operator must publish the closure receipt at completion/revocation and must not mint stage-active authorizations afterward. The runner cannot infer business-stage completion from ledger count alone. Future release approval must include closure as a completion prerequisite.
expiryEnforcementDesign.additionalGuards: Existing current-build/runtime locks remain; candidate deployment changes the locked build. Completion/revocation always wins over an unexpired short authorization.
expiryEnforcementDesign.checks: Before credential access, before each client process/session, existing precommit authorize hook, and before backup acceptance. Expiry triggers rollback/STOP under existing engine rules, not down migration.
